bug_semantics: The project AddFile, EditFile, RemoveFile, and Edit handlers authorize only a namespace-level permission and then trust a body-supplied project or project-file row id. Project.GetData and ProjectFile.GetData select by id alone, so a manager in one namespace can target another namespace's rows, create, overwrite, or delete its files, and replace its repository URL; the URL change runs git remote set-url in the victim project's working tree and can execute attacker-controlled code on a later deployment.
flaw_origin: Commit 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298 first added the four HTTP handlers and their routes. It connected permission-gated requests to id-only Project and ProjectFile lookups without comparing the selected row's namespace_id with gp.Namespace.ID. Its immediate parent contains the model types but none of the four handlers or the git remote set-url path, making this public single-parent commit the smallest surviving Git object that introduces the exploitable mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object has author and committer zhenorzz <zhenorzz@gmail.com>, subject 'U refactor', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: GitHub reviewed advisory GHSA-26rh-24rg-j3vv describes cross-namespace IDOR/RCE in AddFile, EditFile, RemoveFile, and Edit, reports affected versions <= 1.17.5, and is published with withdrawn_at null: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-26rh-24rg-j3vv

CVE Services lookup for CVE-2026-53552 returned state RESERVED rather than REJECTED; the upstream repository nevertheless contains the matching direct fix and a fixed release boundary: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve-id/CVE-2026-53552

At 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298, cmd/server/api/project.go lines 28-45 register /project/edit, /project/removeFile, /project/addFile, and /project/editFile with only EditProject or FileSync permissions; internal/server/route.go lines 60-71 checks permission ids only.

At the BIC, cmd/server/api/project.go lines 409-445 loads Project by body id, updates that id, and runs git remote set-url with the submitted URL; lines 598-632 creates a file from body projectId, lines 644-672 overwrites a file selected by body id, and lines 677-699 deletes a file selected by body projectFileId.

At the BIC, model/ProjectModel.go lines 405-437 implements Project.GetData with Where(id = p.ID), and model/ProjectFileModel.go lines 68-86 implements ProjectFile.GetData with Where(id = pf.ID); neither lookup constrains namespace_id.

git log -L for AddFile, EditFile, RemoveFile, and Edit plus git log -S traces their first public write to 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298; later commit 29ec736e47ddb5033ea294e3ee2f237f0e70da76 is only the 87% path move from cmd/server/api/project.go to cmd/server/api/project/handler.go and is not the BIC.
Direct parent-tree verification against 2dcc8d68d107a8286c4909d7fbe075627e249997 found no func (Project) AddFile, EditFile, RemoveFile, or Edit and no git remote set-url call in any Go file.

The BIC is a single-parent public commit and GitHub's exact commit-to-pulls endpoint returns no associated PR/member history, so no finer public squash members can be reconstructed; decomposed_shas is empty.
Raw git cat-file commit output for 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298 names the same human author and committer and contains only the message 'U refactor', with no AI authorship trailer.

Commit b49eabe903c7d7df1a3763385f5067676da4fdd3 directly adds Project.GetDataInNamespace and ProjectFile.GetDataInNamespace and switches all four advisory handlers to gp.Namespace.ID-scoped lookups; its parent da6091631a60e91369ccbb98135f0efb880f41f6 lacks those checks.

Tag topology: the BIC is absent from v1.12.2 and present from v1.12.3 through v1.17.5; b49eabe903c7d7df1a3763385f5067676da4fdd3 is absent from v1.17.5 and is an ancestor of v1.18.0 (tag commit 4c682981730fb74d599a5cd84a094c5ba6fd4b89), matching the vulnerable and patched boundaries.
reasoning: The advisory mechanism is real and reachable: a caller's namespace grants route permissions, but the affected handlers dereference attacker-selected global row ids and perform filesystem or repository mutations without object ownership authorization. History establishes 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298 as the first write of all four exposed paths; its parent lacks the handlers and RCE sink, while later file-structure commits merely move or edit the surviving code. The direct fix b49eabe903c7d7df1a3763385f5067676da4fdd3 adds namespace-scoped lookups at every named sink and is included in v1.18.0 after vulnerable v1.17.5. AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
